official_questions.stem:
With reference to the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019, consider the following statements about National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) :
I. Judge of the Supreme Court can now be appointed as Chairperson of the Commission.
II. Term of the Chairperson and members shall be three years.
III. Chairperson and members shall be eligible for re-appointment.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
official_questions.core_fact: 2019 amendment: a former CJI or a former SC judge may be Chairperson; term of Chairperson and members 3 years or age 70; eligible for re-appointment; human-rights expert members raised to three.

statements.t: A judge of the Supreme Court can now be appointed NHRC Chairperson.
The term of the Chairperson and members is three years.
The Chairperson and members are eligible for re-appointment.

official_questions.rule: NHRC 2019: CJI or SC judge as chair; 3-year term (or 70); re-appointment allowed; 3 expert members incl. 1 woman.
official_questions.key_note: Initial key only. Strictly, a 'former' SC judge.

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are correct in relation to the Human Rights Commissions in India ?
I. The role to undertake functions relating to human rights in the Union Territory of Ladakh may be conferred upon a State Human Rights Commission by the Central Government.
II. Only 2 persons can be appointed as members of the National Human Rights Commission under the category of possessing knowledge or practical experience with respect to human rights.
III. The President can remove the Chairperson of the State Human Rights Commission on the ground of proved misbehaviour. However, the President has to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court in this matter.
IV. The National Human Rights Commission is not empowered to inquire into any matter after the expiry of two years from the date on which the act constituting violation of human rights is alleged to have been committed.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
official_questions.core_fact: PHRA as amended 2019: Centre may confer UT human-rights functions (other than Delhi) on an SHRC; NHRC has three expert members (one woman); SHRC chair removed by the President after SC inquiry; commissions cannot inquire after one year from the act.

statements.t: Human-rights functions in UT Ladakh may be conferred on an SHRC by the Central Government.
statements.d: Ladakh ... conferred upon a State Human Rights Commission
statements.fact: Per key incorrect. (PHRA s.21(6) as amended lets the Centre confer UT functions – other than Delhi – on an SHRC.)

statements.t: Only two persons can be NHRC members under the human-rights knowledge category.
statements.fact: Three expert members since 2019 (one a woman).

statements.t: The President can remove an SHRC Chairperson for proved misbehaviour after seeking the SC's opinion.
statements.fact: Removal needs an SC inquiry and report, not merely an opinion.

statements.t: NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after two years from the alleged act.
statements.fact: The limitation is one year, not two (s.36(2)).

official_questions.rule: PHRA: 3 expert members, 1-year limitation, removal after SC inquiry, SHRC chair appointed by Governor but removed by President.
official_questions.key_note: Initial key only. Conflict: statement I matches PHRA s.21(6) as amended in 2019 (Centre may confer UT functions, except Delhi, on an SHRC; Ladakh is such a UT). Key 'None' kept.
